title: First BTC long: staged entry, multi-day management, exit around breakeven

pre_trade_context.thesis: Price held despite weak/flat CVD, suggesting possible absorption; confirmation required above 78.15-78.20k.

timeline.state: Price DOWN + CVD DOWN + OI DOWN
timeline.lesson: Treat as deleveraging/position closure first; do not automatically short the liquidation low and do not blindly average a long.

timeline.state: Price UP + CVD slowly UP + OI rapidly DOWN
timeline.lesson: A rebound can be mostly deleveraging/covering rather than fresh trend demand.
A touch or temporary reclaim is not acceptance; prefer hold/retest.

timeline.state: Price UP + CVD FLAT/DOWN + OI DOWN
timeline.lesson: Constructive for an existing long but weak evidence for chasing a new long into resistance.

timeline.state: Price DOWN + CVD DOWN + OI UP
timeline.lesson: Regime changed from deleveraging to bearish leverage expansion; stop treating lower price as an automatic add.

timeline.state: Price DOWN + CVD DOWN + OI UP
timeline.lesson: Loss of support with expanding OI is a risk-off event, not a cheap-price signal.
Exit prevented a thesis-management problem from turning into a larger loss. Once flat, reset and analyze the next setup from zero.

canonical_lessons: Use actual size-weighted average entry, not a simple visual average when tranche sizes differ.
Price/CVD/OI must be interpreted jointly; OI direction alone does not identify long or short side.
Falling OI during a selloff often means deleveraging; rising OI during a selloff is materially more dangerous for a long.
Structural acceptance requires hold/retest, not merely touching a level.
A profitable or breakeven exit is also information: after closure, the next thesis starts from zero rather than inheriting emotional bias.
case_boundary_rule: CASE-001 ends with the 2026-09-08 breakeven exit. All subsequent observations belong to the lead-in and development of CASE-002, not to CASE-001.
